doc.description:
Apply a point deduced by any USHER camera to a flight plan waypoint.
A specialized camera on the MORA companion computer is driven like an ordinary camera: digital_cam_uart_start(CAM) begins its session, digital_cam_uart_stop(CAM) ends it. On stop the camera answers with one geographic point it deduced from that session (USHER_CAM_POINT_RESULT). The reply carries the camera ID, so this module is camera-agnostic: EARcam reports the loudest acoustic spot, and a future camera reporting a point needs no new flight controller code.
Typical flight plan sequence: digital_cam_uart_start(USHER_CAMERA_EARCAM), fly the search pattern, digital_cam_uart_stop(USHER_CAMERA_EARCAM), wait for cam_point_fresh(CAM), then validate the answer, cam_point_to_waypoint(CAM, WP_TARGET), and explicitly cam_point_consume(CAM).
Block exceptions run before the block body, so never stop a camera and test cam_point_fresh() in the same block: command in one block, wait in the next. Only one reply with the matching nonzero session token is accepted after an admitted stop. Duplicate, unsolicited, and delayed previous-session replies are ignored. Start and peer reset invalidate the old answer. A new session token is not reused during the FC runtime, including endpoint switches. cam_point_fresh() becomes true for an accepted VALID or INVALID answer and is cleared only by cam_point_consume(), start, or peer reset. Applying a waypoint does not consume the answer. An INVALID answer retains coordinates for diagnostics but makes cam_point_valid() false. Always test validity.
cam_point_to_waypoint() preserves the waypoint altitude and refuses a point outside the fixed-wing max_dist_from_home rectangular limits before changing any coordinate; rejection leaves the waypoint unchanged. It uses the generated HOME ID and the existing waypoint accessors without modifying common navigation. It returns true on success and consumes the fresh flag; on failure it returns false without consuming the point. Use !cam_point_to_waypoint(CAM, WP_TARGET) in a failure exception. cam_point_within(CAM, WP_REF, radius) is a plausibility gate against a known search area; it bounds where the camera says the point is, and is not evidence that the estimate is accurate. Camera quality values are camera-defined and are not comparable between different camera types. Radius, quality threshold, timeout, retries and fallback remain flight-plan policy. LOOM_cam uses camera ID 2 and repeated USHER_CAM_POINT_UPDATE replies rather than a stopped-session estimate. Each update is independently correlated to a recently requested photo, even after its JPEG acknowledgement. The same validity, freshness, quality and altitude-preserving waypoint helpers apply. LOOM START selects outbound references and STOP selects return matching; there is no final point on STOP. Its current neural matcher is an invalid-only framework stub. See OPENUAS/loom_cam_demo.xml and USHER documentation/loom_cam.md. Start/stop return zero on complete command admission, not camera execution. The demo waits for admission before searching or waiting for a reply.
